title: Iterative invoker: compatibility layer and loop-guard design for multi-tool streaming
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement an iterative invoker layer that safely composes multiple tool/function calls in streaming scenarios while providing compatibility adapters for legacy function-call formats and enforcing structured-output contracts. The invoker must support progressive streaming of tokens and tool responses, deterministic result injection semantics (sanitization and provenance), and robust recursion/loop guards to prevent runaway loops or repeated tool churn. This ticket covers design, a compatibility shim for older SDKs, protocol for tool-result provenance headers, and an experimental runtime flag for hysteresis-based backoff during detected loops.
acceptance_criteria: Invoker can chain 3+ heterogeneous tools in a single streaming session without deadlock or unbounded memory growth
Tool result injection includes provenance metadata (tool_id, call_id, injected_at) and is recorded in trace logs
Compatibility shim translates legacy function-call payloads (v1) to new structured-output schema (v2) with test coverage
Recursion detection triggers a soft-fallback after configurable threshold (default 4 hops) and emits telemetry event execution.loop_detected
E2E tests show <2% latency regression for typical 1-2 tool chains and no increase in error rate in canary environment
technical_decisions: Use a hop-count + content-hash signature as primary loop detector (cheap, stream-friendly)
Inject provenance as small header metadata instead of embedding into tool payloads to keep structured outputs stable
Compatibility adapter lives as a per-session transform step, not a global runtime rewrite, to limit blast radius
Backoff strategy: progressive hysteresis (1s, 2s, 5s) with optional circuit-breaker that returns a structured placeholder response
Streaming boundary markers: explicit token-level markers (START_TOOL / END_TOOL) to help downstream parsers avoid partial-JSON confusion
test_plan: Unit: signature-hash generator, hop-count increments, compatibility transforms
Integration: orchestrate 3 tool types (http tool, db lookup, model-vendor-call) under streaming mode
Chaos: simulate tool that re-injects previous outputs to validate loop detection and backoff
Performance: canary run on dedicated pool - measure p50/p95 latency delta and token throughput
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag invoker_iterative_v2. Start with internal alpha (team=platform), then canary 10% on runtime-1.18 dedicated pools, evaluate telemetry for 2 weeks, expand to 50% then 100%. Provide opt-out via per-customer routing policy.
risks: False positives in loop detection when legitimate repeated tool calls occur (e.g., iterative refinement) - mitigated by content-hash tolerance window
Legacy SDKs that rely on in-band JSON tool outputs may break if boundary markers are misinterpreted
Sanitization may strip necessary fields from third-party tool outputs; need curated allowlist
